es.summary: Alteración neuropsiquiátrica causada por la acumulación de toxinas, principalmente amoníaco, en pacientes con insuficiencia hepática.
key_points: Acumulación de amoníaco y otros neurotoxinas por falla hepática.
Factores precipitantes: infección, sangrado gastrointestinal, constipación, sedación.
Clasificación en grados I‑IV según West Haven.
Tratamiento de primera línea: lactulosa y rifaximina.
Monitoreo de nivel de amoníaco y estado mental.

pathophysiology: El hígado enfermo no convierte amoníaco en urea, aumentando su concentración plasmática.
El amoníaco atraviesa la barrera hematoencefálica y altera la neurotransmisión.
Inflamación cerebral y edema de astroglía reducen la función cognitiva.
Factores precipitantes aumentan la producción o disminuyen la eliminación de amoníaco.
risk_factors: Sangrado gastrointestinal y uso de diuréticos.
Uso de sedantes, benzodiacepinas o anestésicos.
signs_symptoms: Cambios en el nivel de conciencia: somnolencia, confusión, asterixis.
Falta de coordinación motora, temblor de las manos.
Hipertensión portal con ascitis y edema.
diagnostics: Examen neurológico y escala West Haven (I‑IV).
Nivel de amoníaco plasmático > 50 µmol/L (varía por laboratorio).
Pruebas de función hepática: AST, ALT, bilirrubina, INR.
Electrolitos: Na+, K+, Cl‑ en mEq/L; hiponatremia frecuente.
Imágenes (ecografía, tomografía) para descartar hemorragia intracraneal.
treatment: Lactulosa oral o vía rectal para acidificar colon y reducir absorción de amoníaco.
Rifaximina 550 mg cada 12 h para disminuir bacterias productoras de amoníaco.
Corrección de precipitantes: antibióticos, control de sangrado, laxantes.
Restricción moderada de proteínas (0.8 g/kg/día) si está indicado.
Suplementos de zinc y L‑ornitina L‑aspartato en algunos protocolos.
complications: Desnutrición y pérdida de masa muscular.
nursing_care: Evaluar nivel de conciencia cada hora usando escala de Glasgow y West Haven.
Monitorear signos vitales, presión arterial, frecuencia respiratoria y saturación O₂.
Registrar ingesta y eliminación; vigilar estreñimiento y diarrea.
Administrar lactulosa y rifaximina según prescripción; observar diarrea excesiva.
Mantener posición semisentado para prevenir aspiración.
patient_teaching: Explicar objetivo de lactulosa: producir heces blandas y eliminar amoníaco.
Instruir sobre dieta baja en proteínas de alta calidad y evitar ayuno prolongado.
Enseñar signos de empeoramiento: somnolencia creciente, temblor de manos.
Recomendar evitar alcohol y sedantes sin prescripción.
Promover hidratación adecuada y uso de laxantes suaves si es necesario.

evidenced_by: Disminución de la capacidad de concentración
outcomes: Nivel de energía: paciente reporta aumento de energía a 3/10 en 48 h
Actividad: paciente completa actividades de autocuidado sin ayuda en 72 h

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de energía y tolerancia al reposo cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detectar deterioro temprano y ajustar actividades

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso cada 30‑45 min durante actividades
interventions.rationale: Previene agotamiento y reduce riesgo de caída

interventions.action: Fomentar posición semisentada y movilización pasiva de extremidades
interventions.rationale: Mejora perfusión cerebral y reduce asterixis

interventions.action: Administrar lactulosa según orden y registrar consistencia de heces
interventions.rationale: Disminuye amoníaco y mejora claridad mental

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre evitar esfuerzos físicos intensos
interventions.rationale: Previene aumento de la producción de amoníaco

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de perfusión tisular cerebral ineficaz
outcomes: Perfusión cerebral: paciente mantiene presión arterial media ≥ 65 mmHg
Estado mental: escala de Glasgow ≥ 14 en 24 h

interventions.action: Monitorear presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca cada hora
interventions.rationale: Detectar hipotensión que compromete perfusión cerebral

interventions.action: Mantener hidratación adecuada, 30‑35 mL/kg/día
interventions.rationale: Optimiza volumen intravascular y flujo cerebral

interventions.action: Evitar sedación excesiva; usar la menor dosis eficaz de benzodiacepinas
interventions.rationale: Reduce depresión respiratoria y cerebral

interventions.action: Controlar temperatura corporal, mantener 36‑37 °C
interventions.rationale: Previene aumento del metabolismo cerebral

interventions.action: Notificar al médico ante cambios de nivel de conciencia o presión arterial
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana

en.summary: Neuropsychiatric alteration caused by the accumulation of toxins, primarily ammonia, in patients with liver failure.
key_points: Accumulation of ammonia and other neurotoxins due to liver failure.
Precipitating factors: infection, gastrointestinal bleeding, constipation, sedation.
Classification into grades I‑IV according to West Haven.
Monitoring of plasma ammonia level and mental status.

pathophysiology: The diseased liver fails to convert ammonia into urea, increasing its plasma concentration.
Ammonia crosses the blood‑brain barrier and disrupts neurotransmission.
Cerebral inflammation and astroglial edema reduce cognitive function.
Precipitating factors increase production or decrease elimination of ammonia.
risk_factors: Bacterial infections, especially spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.
Gastrointestinal bleeding and use of diuretics.
Use of sedatives, benzodiazepines or anesthetics.
signs_symptoms: Changes in level of consciousness: somnolence, confusion, asterixis.
Portal hypertension with ascites and edema.
Pupils normal, no focal neurological deficits.
diagnostics: Neurological exam and West Haven scale (I‑IV).
Liver function tests: AST, ALT, bilirubin, INR.
Electrolytes: Na+, K+, Cl‑ in mEq/L; hyponatremia common.
Imaging (ultrasound, CT) to rule out intracranial hemorrhage.
treatment: Oral or rectal lactulose to acidify colon and reduce ammonia absorption.
Rifaximin 550 mg every 12 h to reduce ammonia‑producing bacteria.
Correction of precipitants: antibiotics, control of bleeding, laxatives.
Moderate protein restriction (0.8 g/kg/day) if indicated.
Zinc supplements and L‑ornithine L‑aspartate in some protocols.
nursing_care: Assess level of consciousness hourly using Glasgow and West Haven scales.
Monitor vital signs, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and O₂ saturation.
Record intake and output; monitor for constipation and diarrhea.
Administer lactulose and rifaximin as prescribed; watch for excessive diarrhea.
Maintain semi‑upright position to prevent aspiration.
patient_teaching: Explain the goal of lactulose: produce soft stools and eliminate ammonia.
Instruct on a low‑protein diet of high quality and avoid prolonged fasting.
Teach signs of worsening: increasing somnolence, hand tremor.
Recommend avoiding alcohol and unsupervised sedatives.
Encourage adequate hydration and use of mild laxatives if needed.

outcomes: Energy level: patient reports increase to 3/10 in 48 h
Activity: patient completes self‑care activities without assistance in 72 h

interventions.action: Assess energy level and tolerance to rest every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detect early deterioration and adjust activities

interventions.action: Plan rest periods every 30‑45 min during activities
interventions.rationale: Prevents exhaustion and reduces fall risk

interventions.action: Encourage semi‑upright position and passive limb mobilization
interventions.rationale: Improves cerebral perfusion and reduces asterixis

interventions.action: Administer lactulose as ordered and record stool consistency
interventions.rationale: Reduces ammonia and improves mental clarity

interventions.action: Educate patient to avoid intense physical exertion
interventions.rationale: Prevents increased ammonia production

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for ineffective cerebral tissue perfusion
outcomes: Cerebral perfusion: patient maintains MAP ≥ 65 mmHg

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate hourly
interventions.rationale: Detect hypotension that compromises cerebral perfusion

interventions.action: Maintain adequate hydration, 30‑35 mL/kg/day
interventions.rationale: Optimizes intravascular volume and cerebral blood flow

interventions.action: Avoid excessive sedation; use lowest effective benzodiazepine dose
interventions.rationale: Reduces respiratory and cerebral depression

interventions.action: Control body temperature, maintain 36‑37 °C
interventions.rationale: Prevents increased cerebral metabolism

interventions.action: Notify physician of changes in consciousness or blood pressure
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention

key_points.4.quote: A mental status decline accompanying an increase in ammonia level may indicate hepatic encephalopathy.

sections.risk_factors.4.quote: Drug therapy includes benzodiazepines and the nonbenzodiazepine sedatives.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Asterixis, or flapping movements, when the patient holds out the arms

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: Liver function tests may show increased alanine transaminase (ALT) level and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, bilirubin and prothrombin times will be increased, and albumin level decreased.

sections.treatment.4.quote: Treatment may include Antibiotics Lactulose L-ornithine and l-aspartate preparation Zinc Prophylactic intubation to protect from aspiration or respiratory compromise Table 19.10 Hepatic Encephalopathy (Mandiga et al., 2023) Abdominal ultrasound can diagnose cirrhosis , portal hypertension, or thrombus.

sections.complications.1.quote: Without treatment, portal hypertension can cause complications such as variceal bleeding, ascites, hepatorenal syndrome , infection, and cardiomyopathy.

sections.complications.2.quote: A complication of immunosuppression is increased susceptibility to infection.

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Elevating the head of bed also helps with aspiration prevention during meals.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: The provider will order a high-protein, high-calorie diet.
